Polar Semiconductor is a US semiconductor foundry in Bloomington, Minnesota that manufactures power, sensor and automotive-grade chips on 200mm wafers for customers in automotive, industrial and aerospace markets. It earns money through contract wafer manufacturing. It was formerly owned by Sanken Electric and Allegro MicroSystems and was recapitalised in 2024 with a large US CHIPS Act award and private investment, with the Crunchbase total funding at about $298 million. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Polkadot is a blockchain protocol and network (token DOT) created by Gavin Wood, a co-founder of Ethereum, and developed by Parity Technologies and the Web3 Foundation, which is based in Zug, Switzerland. It links many specialised blockchains (parachains) so they can share security and exchange data. Revenue comes from token issuance and treasury rather than product sales; funding includes a 2017 token sale and later raises of about $300 million. Known mainly within crypto and developer circles, with limited general consumer awareness.

CoinDCX is an Indian cryptocurrency exchange headquartered in Mumbai, founded in 2018. It offers an app and website for retail users to buy, sell and trade crypto, plus products such as futures and staking, and earns trading fees. It became India's first crypto unicorn in 2021 with backing from Coinbase Ventures and others, and has raised roughly $247 million in total. It has millions of registered users, runs heavy advertising in India, and has sponsored cricket-related campaigns. Strong consumer brand awareness in India.

EigenLabs is a Seattle-based company behind EigenLayer, a protocol on Ethereum that lets staked ETH be reused (restaking) to secure other networks and services, and EigenCloud, which offers verifiable compute for apps and AI agents. It was founded by Sreeram Kannan, a University of Washington professor, and earns income through its token ecosystem and protocol fees. It has raised about $234 million, with backing from Andreessen Horowitz and Polychain. Crypto-native and developer-focused, with limited mainstream consumer recognition.

LEADRIVE is a power semiconductor company that, per Crunchbase, supplies domestic power chips and related modules and solutions, mainly for electric vehicles and the automotive sector. The input shows an address in Aachen, Germany, but the funding is in Chinese yuan (about CNY 1.57 billion, latest round September 2025), which points to a Chinese-led business with a German presence. Customers are likely vehicle makers and their suppliers. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mondu is an Amsterdam-based fintech, founded in 2021 and with strong roots in Germany, that offers B2B buy-now-pay-later payment terms to online merchants and marketplaces. Merchants embed Mondu at checkout so business buyers can pay on invoice, while Mondu takes the credit risk and pays the seller upfront, charging merchant fees. Customers are mid-sized e-commerce sellers in Europe. Backed by investors such as Valar Ventures and Cherry Ventures, with total funding of about $239 million including debt. B2B, little public brand awareness.

Credix is a Sao Paulo-based fintech that, per Crunchbase, offers a B2B credit platform and buy-now-pay-later style financing for businesses in Latin America. It lets companies and merchants offer credit terms to their business customers and earns fees and interest. Total funding is about $216 million, which includes debt facilities. Likely focused on Brazil and nearby markets. B2B financial service with little consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LayerX is a Tokyo software company founded in 2018 that builds enterprise SaaS for Japanese businesses, notably Bakuraku (expense, invoice and corporate card management) and an AI-based document workflow product, plus blockchain-related services. It sells subscriptions to Japanese companies of all sizes. It has raised about 28.2 billion yen in total, with investors including Goldman Sachs and Mitsui Sumitomo. B2B brand, known among Japanese finance and accounting teams, with little consumer awareness.

TCL Technology is a Chinese electronics and display group in Huizhou, Guangdong (the input shows Guangdong), parent of TCL Corporation brand-related businesses and the display maker TCL CSOT. It makes LCD and OLED panels, TVs, smartphones, appliances and also solar wafers through TCL Zhonghuan. Revenue is in the tens of billions of dollars and the shares are listed in Shenzhen. The TCL brand sells TVs in over 100 countries and is a top-three global TV brand, and TCL has sponsored sport internationally. Strong consumer awareness.

Ualett is a US fintech app, per Crunchbase, offering online cash advances and personal finance tools to consumers, including rent-related payment solutions. It is shown as based in Wilmington, Delaware (a common incorporation address), with total funding of about $206 million, much of which may be debt capacity. Customers are individual consumers, and revenue likely comes from fees and interest. Consumer app with limited brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Validus is a Singapore fintech founded in 2015 that provides SME lending and supply-chain finance across Southeast Asia, using data and AI for credit decisions. It funds small businesses in Singapore, Indonesia and Vietnam, and connects retail investors and institutions as lenders, earning interest and fees. It has raised about $204 million in equity and debt, with backers including Softbank and MUFG. Business-facing financial brand with modest public awareness beyond regional SME circles.

BitFuFu is a Singapore-headquartered bitcoin mining company that offers cloud mining services, letting customers rent hash power, and also runs its own mining operations and hosting. It is a spin-out of the Bitdeer-linked Bitmain ecosystem, controlled by founder Leo Lu, and has been listed on Nasdaq under FUFU since 2024 following a SPAC merger. Customers are crypto investors and retail users globally. Funding shown is about $181 million. Crypto-sector brand with limited mainstream awareness.

Cohere Health is a Boston-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2019, that sells utilization management software which uses AI to speed up prior authorisation between health insurers and care providers. Customers are health plans and provider groups, paying software fees. It has raised about $186 million, with investors such as Deerfield and Longitude Capital. It is B2B with no consumer brand, and should not be confused with the AI firm Cohere.

Hokodo is a London-based fintech that provides B2B buy-now-pay-later and trade credit services for online sellers and marketplaces, mainly in the UK and Europe. Merchants add it at checkout so business buyers get invoice terms, while Hokodo takes the credit risk and earns fees from merchants. Total funding is about $178 million, including debt facilities. B2B, little public brand awareness.

Kent Outdoors is a US company based in New London, Ohio that Crunchbase describes as a platform of action sports and outdoor brands, with about $190 million of recorded funding. It presumably sells products to retailers and consumers and earns revenue from product sales, but the Crunchbase text does not name its brands, size or owners. Customers are likely outdoor and action sports consumers. Brand awareness is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LianLian is a Hangzhou-based Chinese payments company (LianLian Global) that provides cross-border payment, collection and foreign-exchange services, mainly for Chinese e-commerce sellers on Amazon and other marketplaces, and runs domestic mobile payments. It earns transaction and FX fees and holds payment licences in several jurisdictions including the US, EU and Hong Kong. Total funding is about $197 million. B2B and merchant-focused, with little general consumer awareness outside China.

OCN is a Miami-based car subscription company, per Crunchbase, offering online car rentals through all-inclusive monthly subscriptions that bundle the vehicle, insurance and maintenance. Customers are consumers and gig drivers, and revenue comes from monthly subscription fees. Total funding is about $195 million, likely largely vehicle financing. Operates mainly in the US. Consumer service with modest brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Peek is a San Francisco travel technology company, founded in 2014, that operates a booking platform and software for tour and activity operators, plus a consumer marketplace (Peek.com) for booking tours, attractions and experiences in many cities. Revenue comes from software fees and booking commissions. It has raised about $190 million, with investors including Sequoia-related funds and Airbnb alumni backers. Mostly known to tour operators, with growing but limited consumer recognition.

RedotPay is a Hong Kong-based stablecoin payments fintech founded in 2023 that offers a wallet and card letting users hold and spend crypto and stablecoins such as USDT at merchants worldwide, as well as remittances and business payments. Revenue comes from card, transfer and conversion fees. It has raised about $194 million, with backers including Pantera and Goodwater. Users are mainly in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Growing crypto-consumer brand, limited mainstream awareness.

Bumper is a London-based automotive fintech that offers a pay-monthly service for car repairs, servicing and MOT, spreading the cost into instalments through partner garages in the UK and Europe. Customers are motorists, and it earns fees from garages and finance partners. Founded around 2017, it has raised about $168 million including debt facilities. Brand is known among UK motorists and garages through advertising, but is not a mass-market name.

Empathy is a US startup, per Crunchbase, offering a mobile app that guides families through the practical steps after a loved one dies, such as paperwork, accounts and arrangements, along with employer benefit programs. It is based in New York, with total funding of about $162 million. Customers are individuals and employers who offer it as a benefit. Small consumer brand with limited public recognition. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Endowus is a Singapore-based wealth management platform, founded in 2017, that offers digital investment portfolios, unit trusts and private market funds to individuals and families, with cash and CPF retirement money options. It earns advisory and platform fees and operates in Singapore and Hong Kong. Total funding is about $167 million, with investors such as Lightspeed and Prosus. Known in Singapore's retail investing market, with modest awareness elsewhere.

Growatt New Energy is a Shenzhen-based Chinese manufacturer of solar inverters, residential energy storage systems, EV chargers and related monitoring software, founded in 2011. It sells through installers and distributors to homeowners and businesses in over 100 countries and is one of the largest residential inverter makers by shipments. Revenue is in the low billions of dollars. Crunchbase shows about CNY 1.08 billion of funding. The brand is well known to installers and in the solar trade, but consumer awareness is modest.

Hala is a Saudi Arabian digital financial platform, per Crunchbase, offering payments and financial services for consumers and businesses. It is based in Riyadh, has raised about $164 million in total funding, and probably combines digital wallet and payment acceptance services. Revenue likely comes from transaction fees. Brand awareness is mostly within Saudi Arabia. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

MCL Finance is a London-based fintech, per Crunchbase, that provides unsecured SME lending to small businesses in the UK. Its funding figure of about 131 million is probably debt capacity from lenders rather than equity. Customers are small and medium-sized businesses, and it earns interest and fees. B2B lender with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

MoviePass is a US movie-ticket subscription service, launched in 2011 and made famous after Helios and Matheson Analytics bought it in 2017 and cut the price to $9.95 a month, driving millions of subscribers and heavy losses. The service shut in 2019 and the parent company went bankrupt; it was relaunched in a limited form in 2023. Based in New York, with about $171 million raised. Well-known consumer brand, but a troubled and largely defunct business.

World Acceptance Corporation is a Greenville, South Carolina consumer finance company listed on Nasdaq (WRLD), founded in 1962. It makes small instalment loans, typically a few hundred to a few thousand dollars, to subprime borrowers through roughly 1,000 branches in the US and Mexico, earning interest and fees, with revenue of about $600 million a year. It operates under the World and Preferred Credit names. Local consumer lender with limited national brand awareness.

Alleviate Financial is an Irvine, California company that provides consumer debt relief services, such as debt settlement or consolidation, helping people reduce what they owe. The Crunchbase figure of $150 million is probably funding for the lending side. Customers are US consumers with heavy credit card or personal debt, and revenue comes from program fees. Consumer service with modest brand awareness, and marketing for it is likely performance-driven. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

BeatBread is a music funding platform, founded in 2018 and listed in Saint George, Utah, that advances money to independent artists and labels against future royalties and streaming revenue, using data to price deals. Artists keep ownership of their masters. It has raised about $158 million including debt. Customers are musicians and music rights holders, and it earns a share of revenues. Known in the independent music scene, with limited mainstream awareness.

Beehive is a Dubai-based fintech that runs a peer-to-business lending platform, giving small and medium-sized businesses in the UAE and wider Middle East access to financing from investors. It was founded around 2016 and is regulated in Dubai's financial centre. Revenue comes from loan fees and interest spreads, and it has raised about $152 million including debt. B2B and investor-facing, with limited consumer awareness.

Beond is a Dubai-based premium leisure airline, founded in the Maldives and Dubai, which flies business-class style services between Europe, the Middle East and the Maldives using Airbus A319 aircraft with 44 seats. It aims at high-end holidaymakers and sells tickets directly. Total funding is about $155 million, and it launched flights in 2022. It is a niche, small brand with limited awareness outside luxury travel and the Maldives market.

Bitwise is a San Francisco-based crypto asset manager, founded in 2017, which offers index funds and exchange-traded products, including the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index fund, Bitcoin ETF (BITB) and Ethereum ETF. It sells to individuals, advisers and institutions and earns management fees on tens of billions of dollars of assets. It has raised about $155 million in venture funding and was an early mover in spot bitcoin ETFs in the US. Strong in the investor community, with modest mass-market awareness.

Chalo is an Indian mobility app, based in Navi Mumbai and founded in 2017, that provides live tracking of buses and digital ticketing and passes for city transport, working with state bus operators in dozens of Indian cities. Customers are commuters and transport authorities, and revenue comes from ticketing fees and technology services. It has raised about $150 million, with investors including Tiger Global and Prosus. Known to daily bus commuters in India, with growing consumer awareness.

PayU is a payments and fintech business headquartered in Gurugram, India, part of the Prosus group (formerly Naspers). It provides payment gateway and acceptance services to online merchants, as well as consumer and merchant credit through LazyPay, and operates in India and other emerging markets. It earns fees on payment volumes, and the funding shown is about 13 billion rupees. Merchant-facing brand, well known in Indian e-commerce, but consumer awareness is moderate.

Playtomic is a Madrid-based app and software platform, founded in 2015, that lets players find, book and pay for padel, tennis and pickleball courts and join matches with other players, while giving clubs management tools and payments. It operates in more than 40 countries, with thousands of partner clubs, and earns subscription and transaction fees. Total funding is about 137 million. Well known among racket sport players, especially padel, which is fast growing.

KG Mobility is a South Korean car maker based in Pyeongtaek, formerly SsangYong Motor, renamed in 2023 after being taken over by the KG Group. It builds SUVs and pickups such as the Torres, Rexton and Musso, sold in South Korea and exported to Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere, with sales of about 100,000 vehicles a year. It is listed on the Korean exchange (KOSDAQ: 003620). Known as a regional car brand with moderate global consumer awareness.

ADNOC is the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, the state-owned energy group of the United Arab Emirates, headquartered in Abu Dhabi. It produces about 4 million barrels of oil a day, operates gas, refining, petrochemicals and shipping through subsidiaries such as ADNOC Distribution, ADNOC Gas and Borouge, and invests in renewables via Masdar. Customers are global energy buyers and retail fuel customers in the UAE. Its sponsorship profile is established, including in Formula 1 and other sport, and consumer visibility is strong in the Gulf.

Celanese is a Texas-based global chemical and specialty materials company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CE). It produces acetyl chain products, engineered materials, and polymers sold to manufacturers in automotive, medical, filtration, paints and consumer goods, earning about $10 billion of revenue a year. It acquired DuPont's Mobility and Materials business in 2022. Customers are industrial companies worldwide. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness.

Didi is a Chinese mobility platform headquartered in Beijing that runs ride-hailing, taxi, bike-sharing, delivery and car services, plus autonomous driving, with hundreds of millions of annual users in China and expansion in Latin America and elsewhere. It earns commissions on rides and services. It listed in New York in 2021, then delisted in 2022 after Chinese regulatory action, and now trades over the counter. Raised more than $23 billion in total. Very high consumer visibility in China.

Warner Bros. Discovery is a US media and entertainment group headquartered in New York, formed in 2022 by the merger of WarnerMedia and Discovery. It owns Warner Bros. studios, HBO and Max streaming, CNN, TNT Sports, Discovery Channel, Eurosport and many other networks, earning from subscriptions, advertising and content licensing. Listed on Nasdaq (WBD) with revenue of about $40 billion and plans to split into two companies. It holds major sports rights, so it is relevant to advertising and F1-style broadcast partnerships.

Amrize is a Chicago-based building materials company created when Holcim spun off its North American business in June 2025, listed on the New York Stock Exchange and SIX Swiss Exchange (AMRZ). It produces cement, aggregates and ready-mix concrete plus building envelope products such as roofing, serving US and Canadian construction and infrastructure customers, with revenue of about $11 billion. It is a large B2B brand, mostly known to contractors, with little consumer visibility.

Argo AI was a Pittsburgh-based self-driving technology company, founded in 2016 and backed heavily by Ford and Volkswagen, which built autonomous vehicle software, hardware and maps and tested robotaxis in several US cities and Germany. It raised about $3.6 billion in total funding, and in October 2022 Ford and Volkswagen decided to shut it down, absorbing some staff. It is defunct and not a current sponsorship prospect.

Ball Corporation is a Colorado-based packaging company, founded in 1880 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange (BALL), and one of the largest makers of aluminium beverage cans in the world. It supplies drinks brands such as Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and brewers, and also reusable aluminium cups and bottles, with revenue of about $12 billion. It sold its aerospace unit to BAE Systems in 2024. B2B packaging supplier with limited consumer awareness, although it is a known supplier to major drinks brands.

BHP is the world's largest listed mining company, headquartered in Melbourne, with shares listed in Australia (BHP), London and New York. It produces iron ore, copper, metallurgical coal, potash and nickel, selling commodities to steelmakers and manufacturers worldwide, mainly in China, with revenue of about $50 billion a year. It operates large sites in Australia and the Americas. B2B commodity producer with strong corporate profile, but no consumer product brand.

Cainiao Logistics is the logistics arm of Alibaba Group, headquartered in Hangzhou and founded in 2013. It runs a smart logistics network connecting warehouses, couriers and cross-border delivery for Taobao, Tmall and AliExpress merchants, with global parcel and fulfilment services, and earns fees from shippers. Alibaba holds the majority stake and plans to list the company. Consumers know it through its parcel tracking app, but it remains mostly a B2B brand.

Crown Holdings is a Pennsylvania-based metal packaging company, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CCK), which makes aluminium and steel beverage cans, food cans, aerosol containers and closures for brands such as Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and major food companies. It has about 130 plants worldwide and annual sales of about $12 billion. Customers are consumer goods and food companies. B2B packaging supplier with little direct consumer brand awareness.

Grab Financial Group is the financial services arm of Grab, the Singapore-based Southeast Asian super-app. It provides digital payments through GrabPay, consumer and merchant lending, insurance, and a digital bank joint venture, serving Grab's riders, drivers and merchants in markets including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines. It is a subsidiary of Grab Holdings (Nasdaq: GRAB). Grab itself has very high consumer visibility in the region, and this unit benefits from it.

Inspur Cloud is the cloud computing arm of Inspur Group, based in Jinan, Shandong, China. It provides datacenter, public and private cloud, big data and AI services mainly to Chinese government bodies, state enterprises and industrial customers, drawing on Inspur's server hardware business, one of the world's largest server makers. It earns revenue from cloud services and solutions. B2B brand with little consumer awareness, and funding shown is about $3 billion.

Paychex is a Rochester, New York company listed on Nasdaq (PAYX) that offers payroll, human resources, benefits and insurance services to small and mid-sized US businesses, serving about 740,000 clients. It earns recurring service fees and interest on client funds, with annual revenue above $5 billion, and bought Paycor in 2025. It also has strong visibility in US sport as a NASCAR and IndyCar sponsor, so it has a record of sponsorship activity.

PDD Holdings is the parent of Pinduoduo, the Chinese social e-commerce marketplace, and Temu, its international shopping platform launched in 2022 which sells low-priced goods across the US, Europe and other markets. It earns from advertising, merchant fees and transaction services, with revenue above $50 billion. Originally based in Shanghai, it re-domiciled to Ireland in Dublin and is listed on Nasdaq (PDD). Temu is a heavy advertiser, including a major Super Bowl presence, so it has strong consumer visibility.

Redwood Materials is a Carson City, Nevada battery recycling and materials company founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, a Tesla co-founder. It recovers lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper from used batteries and electronics and produces battery materials for cell makers, and also runs Redwood Energy, repurposing old EV batteries for storage. Customers include Panasonic, Toyota and Ford. It has raised about $4 billion. Known in the EV industry, with modest consumer awareness.

Roper Technologies is a diversified technology company based in Sarasota, Florida, listed on Nasdaq (ROP). It owns and acquires niche software and technology businesses, including Deltek, Aderant, Procare and Neptune, selling to government, legal, education, healthcare and utility customers, with revenue of about $7.5 billion. It moved from industrial products to being mainly software over the past decade. Strictly B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Tronox is a Stamford, Connecticut-registered global producer of titanium dioxide pigment, zircon and related chemicals, with mines and plants in Australia, South Africa, Brazil, the US and Europe. It supplies paint, plastics, paper and coatings manufacturers and earns about $3 billion in revenue. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TROX) and operationally led from Stamford and the UK. B2B commodity chemicals supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Trucordia is a US insurance brokerage based in Lindon, Utah, formed through the combination of several regional brokerages and backed by private equity investors, with Crunchbase showing about $5.5 billion in funding including equity and debt. It sells commercial insurance, employee benefits and personal lines, earning commissions and fees from carriers and clients. It grows by acquiring local agencies. B2B and local-agency focused, with limited national brand awareness.

Yuanfudao is a Beijing-based Chinese online education company, founded in 2012, which offers live classes, tutoring and learning apps for K-12 students, including its Yuanfudao and Xiaoyuan Souti apps. It earned money from course fees until China's 2021 crackdown on for-profit tutoring forced it to cut back and shift to smart hardware and other products. It raised about $4 billion in total, and was valued at over $15 billion at its peak. Well known to Chinese families.

Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) is Poland's state-owned national development bank, headquartered in Warsaw, wholly owned by the Polish government. It manages state funds, guarantees and EU programmes, finances infrastructure, housing and local government projects, and supports small companies. It serves government bodies, municipalities and businesses rather than retail customers. Funding shown is about $2.5 billion. Public institution with low consumer visibility.

Bank Mandiri is Indonesia's largest bank by assets, headquartered in Jakarta and majority-owned by the Indonesian government, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BMRI). It offers retail, corporate, SME and digital banking, including the Livin' by Mandiri app, with tens of millions of customers and a presence in Singapore, Hong Kong and elsewhere. A familiar household brand in Indonesia and active in sport and sponsorship locally.

BlueNord is an Oslo-listed oil and gas company (Oslo Bors: BNOR), formerly Norwegian Energy Company, which now focuses on the Danish part of the North Sea after taking over Hess's interest in the Syd Arne field and the Danish Underground Consortium stakes. It sells crude and gas to refiners and traders and pays shareholder dividends. Revenue comes from production of about 25,000-30,000 barrels a day. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Cadeler is a Danish offshore wind installation company, headquartered in Copenhagen, that owns a fleet of specialised jack-up vessels, including large installation ships named after Wind, Orca and Osprey type units, used to build and service wind turbines and foundations. Customers are offshore wind developers and turbine makers such as Orsted and Vestas. Listed in Oslo and on the New York Stock Exchange (CDLR). It merged with Eneti in 2023. B2B contractor with no consumer visibility.

CDB Aviation is a Dublin-based aircraft leasing company and wholly owned subsidiary of China Development Bank Financial Leasing (CDB Leasing). It owns and leases commercial passenger aircraft to airlines worldwide, with a portfolio of several hundred aircraft, and earns lease rental income. Funding shown is about $2.6 billion. Customers are airlines, not consumers. B2B financial and aviation asset business with low public brand awareness.

CEZ Group is the Czech Republic's largest energy company, headquartered in Prague and majority-owned by the Czech state, listed on the Prague Stock Exchange. It generates electricity from nuclear (Temelin and Dukovany), coal, gas and renewables, and distributes power and sells energy to households and business in the Czech Republic, Romania and elsewhere in Central Europe. Revenue is around 10 billion euros or more. Household name in the Czech Republic and a known sponsor of Czech sport.

Compass Group is the world's largest contract catering company, headquartered in Chertsey, UK and listed on the London Stock Exchange (CPG). It runs restaurants and food services for businesses, schools, hospitals, sports venues, defence sites and offices across around 30 countries, through brands such as Levy and Eurest, with revenue of about 40 billion pounds and more than 500,000 employees. Levy provides hospitality at major sporting events. B2B brand with low consumer recognition, but strong in event hospitality.

Deliveroo is a London-based food delivery platform founded in 2013 that connects restaurants, grocers and riders with customers in the UK, Ireland, France, Italy, the UAE, Kuwait and Qatar. It earns commissions, delivery fees and subscription income (Deliveroo Plus). It listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2021 and was acquired by DoorDash in a roughly 2.9 billion pound deal that completed in October 2025. Strong consumer brand and previous sports sponsorships.

DRA Advisors is a New York-based real estate investment manager, founded in 1986, that raises funds for institutional investors such as pension funds and invests in office, industrial, multifamily and retail properties in the US. It earns management and performance fees, and has billions of dollars of assets under management. Funding shown is about $1.7 billion. B2B investment manager with little public brand awareness.

Ellevio is Sweden's largest electricity distribution network company, headquartered in Stockholm. It owns and operates the regional and local power grids supplying about 1000000 customers, including much of Stockholm, and earns regulated network tariffs. It is owned by a group of institutional investors including Alecta, AP3 and Folksam among others, following the earlier sale from Vattenfall. Consumers know it from their grid bill, but it has little brand profile otherwise.

Energy Development Oman (EDO) is a Muscat-based oil and gas company, owned by the Omani state, which holds a stake in Block 61 (the Khazzan and Ghazeer gas fields) alongside BP and has other upstream interests. Revenue comes from gas and condensate sales, mostly to the domestic market. Customers are Omani utilities and industry, not consumers. Funding shown is about $2 billion. B2B energy producer with little public brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Eurowind Energy is a Danish developer, owner and operator of wind and solar power projects, based in Hobro, Jutland, with activities across Europe including Denmark, Germany, Poland and Spain. Revenue comes from electricity sales and from developing and selling energy projects, with total funding of about 2.2 billion. Customers are utilities and grid buyers rather than consumers. B2B brand with low public awareness.

Futu Holdings is a Hong Kong-headquartered online brokerage and wealth management company listed on Nasdaq (FUTU). It runs the Futu NiuNiu app for investors in Hong Kong and mainland China, and Moomoo for customers in the US, Singapore, Australia, Canada and Japan. It earns trading commissions, margin interest and wealth management fees from several million paying clients. Strong retail investor brand in Hong Kong, with growing international marketing.

Garanti BBVA is one of Turkey's largest private banks, headquartered in Istanbul and majority-owned by Spain's BBVA. It provides retail, SME, corporate and digital banking, with several hundred branches, tens of millions of customers, and assets of the order of tens of billions of dollars. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (GARAN). It has long been a sponsor of Turkish sport and arts, and is a household brand in Turkey.

Halkbank (Turkiye Halk Bankasi) is a Turkish state-owned bank headquartered in Ankara and Istanbul, listed on Borsa Istanbul (HALKB). It offers retail, commercial and SME banking, with a focus on small tradespeople and artisans, through hundreds of branches. The state holds the majority through the sovereign wealth fund. It has been involved in a US legal case over sanctions evasion. Well-known domestic consumer bank, with a history of sports sponsorship in Turkey.

ICEYE is a Finnish space technology company in Espoo, founded in 2014, that operates the world's largest constellation of small radar (SAR) imaging satellites, which can see through clouds and at night. It sells imagery and analytics to defence ministries, insurers, disaster response agencies and commercial users, with growing defence demand in Europe. It has raised over $2 billion in funding and is valued at over a billion dollars. B2B and government customers, with low consumer awareness.

Impossible Foods is a Redwood City, California food company, founded in 2011, that makes plant-based meat products such as the Impossible Burger, sausage and nuggets, using a soy leghemoglobin ingredient. It sells through supermarkets and restaurant chains such as Burger King, and operates in the US, Canada, Asia and Europe. Funding is about $1.9 billion from investors including Khosla and Temasek. Strong consumer brand in plant-based food, and has previously sponsored sport.

Intrum is a Stockholm-based credit management company that collects debts and buys non-performing loans for banks, telecom, utility and retail clients across about 20 European countries. It earns fees and returns on purchased portfolios, and has been listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. It carried heavy debt and completed a restructuring in 2024 to cut leverage and extend maturities. B2B, with a low and sometimes negative public profile among consumers.

JD Health is a Chinese online healthcare platform, a subsidiary of JD.com based in Beijing and listed in Hong Kong (6618), which sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs, health products and offers online consultations and family doctor services to consumers across China. Revenue is about 60 billion yuan a year, mainly from product sales and advertising. Consumers use it through the JD app. Strong consumer brand in China via JD.

Just Eat Takeaway.com is an Amsterdam-based online food delivery marketplace, formed in 2020 by the merger of Just Eat and Takeaway.com, operating in the UK, Germany, Netherlands, Canada and other European markets. It earns commissions and delivery fees from restaurants and orders. It was acquired by Prosus in a 4.1 billion euro deal that completed in 2025 and was delisted. Strong consumer brand in Europe, with substantial sports sponsorship history.

Lalamove is a Hong Kong-headquartered on-demand logistics platform, founded in 2013, that connects customers and small businesses with van, truck and motorbike drivers for same-day delivery and moving across Asia, Latin America and elsewhere. It earns commissions on orders and operates in about 30 markets with millions of drivers. Funding is about $2.5 billion, with investors including Sequoia and Hillhouse. Well-known consumer-facing brand in Asian cities.

Marlette Funding is a Wilmington, Delaware company that operates Best Egg, a US online personal loan platform that offers unsecured personal loans and credit card products to consumers, often for debt consolidation. It earns interest and fees, with loan volume of billions of dollars a year, and is owned by Marlette Holdings, backed by private equity and bank partners including Cross River and Fortress-related interests. Best Egg has substantial US consumer marketing and advertising.

National Bank of Greece is the oldest and one of the largest Greek banks, founded in 1841 and headquartered in Athens, listed on the Athens Stock Exchange (ETE).
